source_lines.text: cc536-main-live-method
SOURCE_1

These six-market daily-bar base rates include asset drift: in the audited November 2016 to November 2026 sample a zero-net-mean 2,000-draw 60-calendar-day block test produced 0.98 PAID_BOTH_HALVES rows out of 54 by chance on average (95% range 0 to 3), versus 5 observed. Choosing rows on the first five years and starting flat on the last five selected 3 rows: 2 stayed positive over 362 test trades at +0.100R per trade, a retrospective dependent sample at a uniform cost of 0.05 normal day with futures roll risk and D1 path uncertainty, not a prospective probability.

Daily bars; R is the stop distance; cost 0.05 of a normal day (D1 ATR14) per round trip; a decision at a close is entered at the next open; inside one bar the stop is taken before the target; one trade at a time per market and behaviour. t is the mean over its standard error using sample standard deviation (nominal IID, not a dependence-adjusted significance claim). Halves split at the fixed midpoint of the calendar window, not the median trade. BTC sessions include weekends; futures are unadjusted continuous proxies with roll risk. Signed oil prices are retained; pending entries use decision-close ATR and include the fill bar.
### Inputs and clocks
For each market select the newest `known_epoch` D1 capture of its named Yahoo series; break ties by descending
`source_id`. `--source-manifest` pins the IDs in its `markets` map instead. Read bars in `open_epoch` order.
Require finite OHLC and `low <= min(open, close) <= max(open, close) <= high`; invalid rows raise market and date.
Signed continuous-futures prices are retained, including the two April 2020 oil bars. Spot FX and BTC prices
must be positive. Remove non-BTC Sundays by `session_date`, not UTC opening weekday. Keep all Bitcoin days.
There is no roll adjustment or imputation. Bulk capture-known-at is not original historical availability.
At completed close index `i`, normal day `A[i]` is the simple mean of the last 14 true ranges, including `i`:
`TR[j] = max(high[j]-low[j], abs(high[j]-close[j-1]), abs(low[j]-close[j-1]))`.
First ATR is at index 14. This is not Wilder smoothing. Signals are decided after close `i`.
The yardstick is UP (+1) if all four differences below are strictly positive, DOWN (-1) if all are strictly
negative, otherwise MIXED (0); it is 0 before index 60:
`close[i]-close[i-20]`, `close[i]-close[i-60]`, `close[i]-mean(close[i-19:i+1])`,
`close[i]-mean(close[i-49:i+1])`. `sign(x)` is +1, -1 or 0.

The side file splits each two-sided behaviour by LONG and SHORT. Each trend row has an always-long comparison. In gold and the S&P 500, being long at all paid as much as being long with the trend. EURUSD and USDJPY results wait for the repaired daily closes. Construction comparisons pool both sides together.
